portInfo.description: Marigot is the main town on the French collectivity of Saint-Martin in the northeast Caribbean. It is not the same call as Philipsburg on Dutch Sint Maarten—confirm your itinerary lists Marigot or Saint-Martin on the French side. The Établissement Portuaire de Saint-Martin (Port of Saint-Martin) handles cruise ships through anchorage and tender landings, with the ferry terminal and Marina Fort Louis on the Marigot waterfront.
portInfo.location: Baie de la Potence / Galisbay, Saint-Martin (French side of the island shared with Sint Maarten)
portInfo.language: French; English widely used in tourism and shops
portInfo.currency: Euro (EUR); US dollars are often accepted—confirm change policies ashore

facts.established: The Port of Saint-Martin (Établissement Portuaire) has supplied the French side by sea since 1995 (port authority public site).
facts.significance: French-side cruise and ferry gateway; commercial quay, ferry links to Anguilla and Saint-Barthélemy, and Marina Fort Louis on the waterfront
culturalHighlights: French Caribbean town centre with open-air markets when operating
Waterfront dining and duty-free shopping zones
Easy day-trip context to nearby islands only when ferry schedules and your all-aboard time allow

size.portCapacity: Commercial port with more than 250 m of quay; cruise operations use anchorage and landings per the port authority
size.annualVisitors: Port of Saint-Martin public information references 200,000+ passengers annually in ferry-terminal context—confirm current totals with the port authority
size.citySize: Marigot is the capital of the French collectivity of Saint-Martin on a shared island with Dutch Sint Maarten

climate.rainySeason: Heavier showers possible May through November (hurricane season awareness)
climate.description: Tropical Caribbean weather—plan shade and hydration for uphill walks such as Fort Louis.

politics.stability: Ordinary urban and tourism awareness applies; check local notices if weather or events affect tender operations.
politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality and whether you stay on the French side only or also cross to Dutch Sint Maarten. Rules change—confirm with official French government travel guidance and your cruise line before you sail.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry the passport or ID documents your cruise line lists for every port of call. Informal open-border movement between French Saint-Martin and Dutch Sint Maarten still requires acceptable ID if authorities ask.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Confirm your sailing's arrival details: Marigot calls use anchorage and tender landings coordinated by the Port of Saint-Martin, not the large Philipsburg cruise piers on the Dutch side. Follow gangway and tender instructions from your ship each day.
gettingThere.distanceToCity: The port authority states cruise anchorage and landings are about 10 minutes from the center of Marigot—actual time depends on tender point, queues, and mobility.
gettingThere.distanceAnswer: Port of Saint-Martin public information cites about 10 minutes from central Marigot after cruise landings; tender location and crowds change that in practice.
gettingThere.walkingTime: From many landings, the Marigot waterfront and lower town are often walkable if you are mobile—Fort Louis adds a steep uphill segment.
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Taxis and informal transport serve Marigot; agree on destination and return timing, and keep payment options your driver accepts.
gettingThere.publicTransport: There is no standard cruise-shuttle contract—use ship tenders first. Trips toward Philipsburg or Dutch-side beaches involve border crossing and separate transport planning.

thingsToDo.intro: A Marigot call is usually a compact French-side day: harbour front, shopping streets, and Fort Louis views—unless your ship sells a Dutch-side or island-wide excursion instead.
topThings: Marigot waterfront and harbour promenade near the ferry terminal
Fort Louis (uphill; allow time, water, and heat margin)
Marina Fort Louis and harbour views
Waterfront cafés and duty-free shopping streets
Inter-island ferries (Anguilla, Saint-Barthélemy) only with confirmed schedules and all-aboard buffer
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay on the Marigot waterfront and skip Fort Louis if heat or tender timing is tight.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Waterfront stroll plus Fort Louis or a relaxed lunch is realistic when landings are close to town and return tenders run on schedule.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A Dutch-side beach or Philipsburg run is possible but eats time for border crossing and transport—only if your French-side window and ship timing allow.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Confirm your sailing's arrival details before booking independent transport. All-aboard time matters more than map distance on tender days.
